title.narrative: Integrated Emergence /Early Recovery Programme for North East Nigeria EA31 2016

description.narrative: In Nigeria, Yobe and Borno states were the worst affected States. The proposed programme will target IDPs, Returnees and the host communities in 2 Local Government Areas (LGAs) in Borno State, Hawul and Askira Uba LGAs. These two LGAs were selected due to the high number of returnees and IDPs coupled with the acute needs and gaps in coverage. These LGAs have been classified as being in phase 3 of food and nutritional insecurity by the cadre harmonize analysis and classification published in August 2016. Though Hawul and Askira Uba are now reasonably accessible to Humanitarian actors, there is still very little presence of humanitarian actors providing relief services in these LGAs. These LGAs fall under the Catholic Diocese of Maiduguri, as such the rapid needs assessment was carried out in close collaboration with JDPC Maiduguri team. While nationally 7.4% of women aged 15-49 years have acute malnutrition, in Borno and Yobe this is respectively 15% and 20%. This translates into 180,707 women in Borno and 131,583 in Yobe being malnourished. The current sources of water include 80% wells and 20% boreholes and hand-pumps. It is important to note that in these communities, the aquifer is very low. The depth runs from depths of 120 metres. As such, the construction of boreholes and hand-pumps may be difficult. Wells that are in use usually dry up between February – May annually. In the communities there are only 12 boreholes, out of which, only one is functional. In addition, the extant sources of drinking water are Hand-pumps and wells. These water sources are not treated. Water is not available at all times. Walk to the water sources are safe for everyone and are at maximum 2-3 kilometres Our proposed response aims to Increase access to water for 9,000 people through the rehabilitation of damaged WASH infrastructure (especially boreholes) and the conversion of some from Generator powered borehole to Solar motorized in communities. Increase access to latrines for 9000 people, alongside hygiene promotion activities using the school and community-led total sanitation approach (SLTS and CLTS). Distribution of Water, hygiene and dignity kits (Jerry cans, buckets, kettles, dignity kits, soap, tooth paste, tooth brush and water guard), Water quality control of existing water sources (test and disinfection of water source) and establishment of WASHCOMS to ensure sustainability with regards to the operation and maintenance of WASH infrastructure.
